lines: +# description: Benchmark of column pruning after statistics propagation removes a redundant filter
+SELECT grp, count(*) FROM events WHERE uuid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY grp ORDER BY grp;
//! Derive output statistics of a monotone function by evaluating it at the corners of its
//! The map of CTE index -> statistics of its definition
-	//! Whether a statistics callback removed aggregate children, leaving columns that may now be unused
+	//! Whether any expression, filter or join condition was removed, leaving columns that may now be unused
//! Node stats for the current node
//! Whether statistics changed which relations a filter depends on
// DML CTEs can invalidate the table statistics captured during planning.
-	// COUNT(x) becomes COUNT(*) during statistics propagation, leaving unreferenced columns in the scan
+	// statistics propagation removes filters, join conditions and aggregate children that it proves redundant.
+	// this can leave columns in a scan that nothing references any more - prune them again
// coalesce child cannot have NULL entries
// filter is always true; it is useless to execute it
// if there is a projection map, we should keep the filter
// filter is always true; it is useless to execute it
// there are multiple conditions: erase this condition
// this is the only condition and it is always true: all conditions are true
+# description: Statistics propagation prunes columns whose only reference was a removed expression
+# the second pruning pass runs on a plan that already carries projection maps
+CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT i AS positive_ints, repeat('x', 100) || i AS never_null_text, i % 7 AS small_ints FROM range(2000) t(i);
+# one row, so its statistics are exact and every t.positive_ints exceeds negative_int
+CREATE TABLE one_row AS SELECT -1 AS negative_int, 3 AS small_int;
+# EXPLAIN cannot see a dangling column: a column read only for a filter is projected out of the scan immediately,
+# so it appears in neither Projections nor Filters. Count the scan's read set from the serialized plan.
+    FROM (SELECT json_serialize_plan(q::VARCHAR, optimize := true) AS plan)
+# filters proved always true are removed and their columns with them, once as table filters in the scan (propagate_get)
+# and once with pushdown off, where they stay above the scan in a filter (propagate_filter, propagate_conjunction)
+       scan_columns('SELECT small_ints FROM t WHERE never_null_text IS NOT NULL'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT small_ints FROM t WHERE positive_ints >= 0'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT small_ints FROM t WHERE positive_ints > 500'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT small_ints FROM t WHERE positive_ints > 500 AND never_null_text IS NOT NULL'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT small_ints FROM t WHERE positive_ints > 500 OR never_null_text IS NOT NULL')
+# a COALESCE argument after one that cannot be NULL is dropped (propagate_operator)
+# an always true join condition is removed and its columns with it, for every join type (propagate_join):
+SELECT scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t JOIN       one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t LEFT JOIN  one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t RIGHT JOIN one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t FULL JOIN  one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t SEMI JOIN  one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int'),
+       scan_columns('SELECT t.small_ints FROM t ANTI JOIN  one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int')
+# results are unaffected by the optimizers
+SELECT sum(small_ints) FROM t WHERE never_null_text IS NOT NULL AND positive_ints > 500
+SELECT count(*), sum(t.small_ints) FROM t JOIN one_row ON t.small_ints = one_row.small_int AND t.positive_ints > one_row.negative_int
+SELECT count(*), sum(a.small_ints) FROM t a LEFT JOIN t b ON a.positive_ints = b.positive_ints WHERE b.never_null_text IS NOT NULL AND b.small_ints > 3
